analysis.title: Bond Traders Hunt For The "Biting Point" As OpenAI's $20 Billion "Apples-To-Oranges" Scare Sends AI CDS To Records
key_insights: Goldman's Macro Roadmap (Rikin Shah, Cosimo Codacci-Pisanelli) argues Treasury yields keep rising until AI borrowers become rate-sensitive or another part of the economy breaks. Nasdaq has barely moved despite the rate rise.
This year's Treasury selloff is almost entirely real-rate driven: 98bp of the 108bp rise in 10Y yields. US 30Y real yields are 3.33%, around the top of the post-2010 range.

Supply is not slowing: fiscal consolidation looks far-fetched and AI capex is projected above $1tn next year. Shah says history says current levels are a buy but there is no obvious catalyst for a reversal.
Shah sees two exits: a repricing lower in the ROI of AI investment, or a change in the cyclical outlook if the K-shaped economy deteriorates more sharply.
Market breadth has split. Since Aug 27 the S&P 500 is +1.28% while the S&P ex-AI is -5.19%. The Russell 2000 has underperformed NDX in 16 of the last 20 sessions, by about 9pp cumulatively.
On Thursday the S&P fell 47bp to 7,765 and the Nasdaq 100 fell 139bp, yet about 70% of S&P members finished up (Goldman's Contessa and Washington).

Nomura's McElligott describes a 'rolling correction' outside the megacaps. Over 30 days REITs are -9.8%, Materials -7.9%, Financials -7.7%. 85% of S&P names are more than 10% below their highs, 59% more than 20% below, 17% down by half.

Goldman equity derivatives (Adrien Simonet) reports crowding: Mag7 is about 22% of US prime exposure, the highest since early 2022. Semis doubled to about 12% from about 6%. About $115bn sits in levered semis ETFs.

The FT reported OpenAI annualized revenue near $50bn at end-September versus the $68-70bn widely cited. ORCL fell 5-6%, NVDA and AMD lost more than 3%, and Goldman's cash desk saw long-only and hedge fund selling in large-cap tech.

Goldman TMT's Sean Johnstone says the gap is a net vs gross reporting difference. OpenAI reports net of cloud partner sales and Anthropic closer to gross. On OpenAI's own basis, progression was nearer $30-50bn than $40-70bn, still roughly 70% growth. He wrote 'many do not adjust'.
Bloomberg reports OpenAI still expects at least $70bn annualized revenue by year-end. SoftBank's Son is seeking up to $100bn from Gulf investors for AI (FT).

Credit did not recover like equities. Oracle 5Y CDS closed at a record 261bp, up 36% on the month. Broadcom 5Y CDS printed a record 136bp. Nearly $500bn of 2026 AI-related borrowing is being repriced.

Goldman credit strats (Reid Zhou) at Thursday's close: CCC spreads 1,014bp (widest in at least three years, +224bp in three months), HY spreads 310bp (+43bp in a month), IG index yield 6.43%. The VIX closed at 15.4, 17th percentile of the past year.

Simonet pitches $859mn of 6-month best-of puts across 29 AI and AI-adjacent names, with basket implied vol in the 6th percentile of the past year. Hedge fund nets are in the 2nd percentile on a 5-year lookback, which he says should contain broad index drawdowns.

Fed Governor Waller anticipates additional hikes, which Goldman economists read as two more, to 4.25-4.50%. 3-month annualized core PCE is 2.0%. Waller cited AI buildout raising high-tech consumer prices. Goldman still expects one more hike, in December.

The article's own view is that the biting point is likely already showing up in AI funding costs (Oracle and Broadcom CDS, CCC spreads) rather than in rates directly. The next test is CPI, which Simonet calls the near-term trigger, after earnings kickoff.

tension_points.bull_case: Nasdaq is resilient because expected AI ROI is easily double digits, so a 50-100bp rise in funding costs does little to slow borrowing. Hedge fund nets are low, OpenAI is still growing about 70%, and Nomura sees the pain trade into earnings as higher.
tension_points.bear_case: The cohort is crowded and shares one risk, the discount rate. Oracle and Broadcom CDS are at records, CCC spreads exceed 1,000bp, and the trade is priced off unaudited private-company run-rates that many investors do not adjust.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A repricing lower in the ROI of AI-related investment or a deterioration in the cyclical outlook from the K-shaped economy. CPI is flagged as the near-term trigger.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman TMT says it was a net vs gross confusion, not a growth collapse, and Bloomberg reports OpenAI still expects at least $70bn annualized revenue by year-end.
tension_points.bear_case: Credit did not accept the clarification. Oracle and Broadcom CDS stayed at records, and until both labs are public or use consistent metrics, this apples-to-oranges volatility is likely to persist.
tension_points.what_invalidates: OpenAI failing to reach at least $70bn annualized revenue by year-end.
